We publish only grouped cells with at least ten reports. We do not publish exact timestamps, individual cities or hospital names. Closed monthly groups are used to reduce the chance of identifying someone. Erasing a report also withdraws the affected public group; raw reports expire after one year.

Keep the deletion code given after submission. It is the proof needed to erase your report without collecting your identity. If you lose it, we cannot reliably identify the report; the retention period still applies. Erasure cannot recall copies someone already downloaded.

NL-48 is an insurer's public disclosure of health-service turnaround times. We transcribe the published cashless pre-authorisation and discharge buckets for each TPA and for individual/group policies. These are the insurer's reported figures, not a patient survey or an independent compliance audit.
What this does and does not show
The 2–6 hour bucket straddles the three-hour discharge deadline. We do not estimate the share decided before or after three hours.
The disclosure clock starts when the TPA receives the discharge bill. Family-entered submission times may capture a different point.
Rows with different TPAs, periods, policy types or units are not combined. Percentages are copied without renormalising rounding.
A sample size is shown only when the exact cashless denominator is identifiable. A missing denominator is not zero.
Missing, scanned, malformed and inconsistent filings are tracked explicitly. Coverage is incomplete and has no market-wide ranking.
Patient reports are voluntary and unverified. Every published cell must contain at least ten reports. Small cells, individual timestamps and hospital names are never displayed.

Each row records its source URL, PDF page, insurer, TPA, period, unit and retrieval date. The repository contains a reproducible transcription pipeline, source hashes, exclusions and spot-check evidence.
